70976-the-radiant-city.description: A book by Evelyn R. Garratt,. are those which probably the conscience of every reader will recognize. An important and valuable feature is the constant reference to the "Guide Book." It has just the teaching to be put into the hands of young people entering life, and yet has ample lessons for their elders. "It shone with a radiance like that of a very precious  stone, such as Jasper, bright and transparent."   —Rev.

arxiv-2102-01636.title: Adaptive Random Bandwidth for Inference in CAViaR Models
arxiv-2102-01636.creator: Alain Hecq, Li Sun
arxiv-2102-01636.description: Abstract This paper investigates the size performance of Wald tests for CAViaR models ( Engle and Manganelli, 2004 ) . We find that the usual estimation strategy on test statistics yields inaccuracies. Indeed, we show that existing density estimation methods cannot adapt to the time-variation in the conditional probability densities of CAViaR models.

arxiv-2110-14576.title: Kripke-Joyal forcing for type theory and uniform fibrations
arxiv-2110-14576.creator: Steve Awodey, Nicola Gambino, Sina Hazratpour
arxiv-2110-14576.description: Abstract . We introduce a new method for precisely relating algebraic structures in a presheaf category and judgements of its internal type theory. The method provides a systematic way to organise complex diagrammatic reasoning and generalises the well-known Kripke-Joyal forcing for logic. As an application, we prove several properties of algebraic weak factorisation systems considered in Homotopy Type Theory.

arxiv-2112-07022.title: Learning Body-Aware 3D Shape Generative Models
arxiv-2112-07022.creator: Bryce Blinn, Alexander Ding, R. Kenny Jones, Manolis Savva, Srinath Sridhar, Daniel Ritchie
arxiv-2112-07022.description: Abstract The shape of many objects in the built environment is dictated by their relationships to the human body: how will a person interact with this object? Existing data-driven generative models of 3D shapes produce plausible objects but do not reason about the relationship of those objects to the human body.

arxiv-2205-07483.title: Three-loop topology analysis of neutral B-meson mixing with tapir
arxiv-2205-07483.creator: Marvin Gerlach
arxiv-2205-07483.description: Abstract Modern advances in particle physics depend strongly on the usage of reliable computer programs. In this context two issues become important: The usage of powerful algorithms to handle the amount of evaluated data properly, and a software architecture capable to overcome the problems of maintainability and extendability. We present our approach to such a computer program, called tapir .

arxiv-2301-12534.title: Vicarious Offense and Noise Audit of Offensive Speech Classifiers: Unifying Human and Machine Disagreement on What is Offensive
arxiv-2301-12534.creator: Tharindu Cyril WeerasooriyaRochester Institute of Technology cyril@mail.rit.edu, Sujan DuttaRochester Institute of Technology sd2516@rit.edu Tharindu RanasingheAston University t.ranasinghe@aston.ac.uk Marcos ZampieriGeorge Mason University mazgla@rit.edu Christopher M. HomanRochester Institute of T
arxiv-2301-12534.description: Abstract ! This paper discusses and contains content that is offensive or disturbing. Offensive speech detection is a key component of content moderation. However, what is offensive can be highly subjective. This paper investigates how machine and human moderators disagree on what is offensive when it comes to real-world social web political discourse.

arxiv-2402-11636.title: Untangling Strongly and Weakly Interacting Configurations in Many-electron Wave Functions
arxiv-2402-11636.creator: J. C. Greer
arxiv-2402-11636.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by J. C. Greer. Accurate solution of the many electron problem including correlations remains intractable except for few electron systems. Describing interacting electrons as a superposition of independent electron configurations results in an apparent combinatorial scaling to achieve an accurate solution. Many approximate approaches for large systems have been introduced, yet controlling and quantifying the error remains a significant hurdle for comparison to experiment. Perturbation calculations are a popular means to estimate neglected energy contributions but give rise to two unanswered questions.

arxiv-2404-14970.title: Integrating Heterogeneous Gene Expression Data through Knowledge Graphs for Improving Diabetes Prediction
arxiv-2404-14970.creator: Rita T. Sousa, Heiko Paulheim
arxiv-2404-14970.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Rita T. Sousa, Heiko Paulheim. Diabetes is a worldwide health issue affecting millions of people. Machine learning methods have shown promising results in improving diabetes prediction, particularly through the analysis of diverse data types, namely gene expression data. While gene expression data can provide valuable insights, challenges arise from the fact that the sample sizes in expression datasets are usually limited, and the data from different datasets with different gene expressions cannot be easily combined.

arxiv-2412-09726.title: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Gaussian Score Approximation for Diffusion Models and its Applications
arxiv-2412-09726.creator: Binxu Wang binxu_wang@hms.harvard.edu, John J. Vastola john_vastola@hms.harvard.edu
arxiv-2412-09726.description: Abstract Diffusion models have achieved remarkable results in multiple domains of generative modeling. By learning the gradient of smoothed data distributions, they can iteratively generate samples from complex distributions, e.g., of natural images. The learned score function enables their generalization capabilities, but how the learned score relates to the score of the underlying data manifold remains largely unclear.

arxiv-2412-12638.title: Fisher information and quantum entropies of a 2D system under a non-central scalar and a vector potentials.
arxiv-2412-12638.creator: Ahmed Becir, Mustafa Moumni
arxiv-2412-12638.description: Abstract We study a two-dimensional system influenced by a non-central potential consisting of a Kratzer potential with a dipole moment, along with a vector potential of the Aharonov-Bohm (AB) effect. We explore various information-theoretic measures, including Fisher information, Shannon entropy, Tsallis entropy, and Renyi entropy.

pmc-10605376.title: PACAP–Sirtuin3 alleviates cognitive impairment through autophagy in Alzheimer’s disease
pmc-10605376.creator: Qing Wang, Yue Wang, Shiping Li, Jiong Shi
pmc-10605376.description: BackgroundAutophagy is vital in the pathogenesis of neurodegeneration. Thus far, no studies have specifically investigated the relationship between pituitary adenylate cyclase-activating polypeptide (PACAP) and autophagy, particularly in the context of Alzheimer’s disease (AD). This study used in vitro and in vivo models, along with clinical samples, to explore interactions between PACAP and autophagy in AD.

pmc-12445563.title: Comparative evaluation of the effect of Snoezelen Distraction Technique on children with Autism and healthy children during dental treatment
pmc-12445563.creator: Sanjna K Sreenivasan, Nikita Lolayekar, Kavita Rai, Aishani Baksi, Kripa Dutta, Manju R
pmc-12445563.description: AimTo compare the effect of Snoezelen distraction technique (SDT) on children with Autism disorder and healthy uncooperative children during dental treatment.Methodology: 17 children diagnosed with Autism (Group 1) and 17 uncooperative healthy children (Group 2) requiring dental treatment were considered for the study. The study comprised of two appointments during which physiological and behavioural parameters were recorded.

pmc-12619072.creator: Daisuke MATSUMOTO, Mako MINE, Norito ISHII, Daisuke TSURUTA, Sho HIROYASU
pmc-12619072.description: atitis, and bronchiolitis obliterans. These diverse manifestations are likely driven by autoantibodies targeting a broad range of autoantigens, including plakin family proteins (envoplakin, periplakin, desmoplakin I/II, BP230), desmogleins (Dsg1/3), desmocollins (Dsc1-3), and collagen XVII (COL17, BP180). While the precise pathology of PNP remains unclear, characterizing the detailed autoantigen profile and its temporal dynamics may provide important mechanistic insights.

pmc-12654813.title: Microbial Interventions for Inflammatory Skin Diseases: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Atopic Dermatitis and Psoriasis
pmc-12654813.creator: Yamil Liscano, Daniel Muñoz Morales, Fernanda Suarez Daza, Sinthia Vidal Cañas, Darly Martinez Guevara, Esteban Artunduaga Cañas, Zhe-Xue Quan
pmc-12654813.description: Inflammatory dermatological diseases represent a significant global health burden, with emerging evidence suggesting that modulation of the gut–skin axis microbial interventions may offer therapeutic benefits. However, current evidence is fragmented, with considerable heterogeneity limiting definitive conclusions. A systematic review and a meta-analysis were conducted following PRISMA guidelines, registered in PROSPERO (CRD42024629809).

Congenital scoliosis is caused by abnormal vertebral development during embryogenesis, often involving incomplete formation or segmentation of vertebrae.

pmc-12816387.title: Genomic characterization, antimicrobial resistance, and virulence profiling of Escherichia coli isolated from diarrheic calves in Gansu, China
pmc-12816387.creator: Qi Meng, Liang Chang, Shengming Wang, Guopeng Lu
pmc-12816387.description: IntroductionThis study provides a comprehensive genomic investigation of Escherichia coli isolated from diarrheic calves in Gansu Province, China, a region with significant livestock production.MethodsWe employed whole-genome sequencing on 15 isolates from 15 different farms to characterize their molecular subtypes, plasmid repertoires, virulence gene profiles, and antibiotic resistance mechanisms.

pmc-13191973.title: Short-term detraining in semi-professional male football players: impact of a 5-day mid-season break on performance - an observational study
pmc-13191973.creator: João G Saldanha, Francisco Santos, Diogo V Martinho, Hugo Sarmento, Adilson Marques, Pedro Campos, Krzysztof Przednowek, Élvio R Gouveia
pmc-13191973.description: BackgroundDetraining is a partial reduction or total stoppage of training workloads, resulting in physical and physiological modifications. Prior studies have shown significant reductions in strength and power typically after long-term interruptions (i.e., > 4 weeks), whereas evidence for short-term detraining (i.e., < 4 weeks) remains inconclusive.

pmc-13392066.creator: Parisa Esmatian, Saeideh Ebrahimiasl, Sudabeh Davaran
pmc-13392066.description: In this study, magnetic iron oxide (Fe2O4) nanoparticles with an inverse spinel structure were synthesized via the co-precipitation method under both thermal and hydrothermal conditions using Fe (II) and Fe (III) chlorides as precursors. The effects of parameters such as temperature and solvent type were investigated. Sodium hydroxide, were used as alkaline agents to adjust the pH during synthesis.

pmc-13486347.title: Dietary Intake Modifies the Association between Air Pollution and Chronic Diseases: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
pmc-13486347.creator: Ye Chen, Bangqin Cai, Fei Wang, Hongyu Xuan, Yongqiang Sun, Yang Xia, Yuhong Zhao, Lishen Shan, Hehua Zhang
pmc-13486347.description: Interaction effects between dietary factors and air pollutants remain inconsistent. This systematic review and meta-analysis examined whether dietary intake modifies the air pollution–chronic disease risk association. This study searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane from inception to May 2026.

pmc-13659240.title: Fast, flexible gene cluster family delineation with IGUA
pmc-13659240.creator: Martin Larralde, Josefin Blom, Hadrien Gourlé, Hale-Seda Radoykova, Lucas Paoli, Georg Zeller, Laura M Carroll
pmc-13659240.description: Prokaryotic genomes harbor a variety of functional elements encoded as contiguous multi-gene clusters. To identify homologous gene clusters, computational tools that account for multi-gene architectures are needed to group gene clusters into Gene Cluster Families (GCFs). However, existing GCF delineation methods do not scale well to large datasets and are often limited to certain subclasses of gene clusters.

(a) Definitions In this Act: (1) Federal land The term “Federal land” means— (A) land of the National Forest System (as defined in section 1609(a) of title 16) administered by the Secretary of Agriculture, acting through the Chief of the Forest Service; and (B).
